infiltration.title: Can this site use infiltration?
infiltration.intro: Establish the ground evidence before relying on infiltration or moving down the destination hierarchy.

screen.question: What does the initial site evidence show?
options: A site constraint may rule it out

initial.text: Review mapping, available investigations, geology, groundwater, contamination and stability. Initial mapping can inform whether further investigation is necessary; it is not proof of a detailed infiltration design.

links.label: IG-01 · Prove infiltration with site testing
RD-02 · Evidence for using a lower destination

constraint.question: Is the reason for discounting infiltration supported by site evidence?
options: Yes — the evidence explains the constraint

discount.result: Record the constraint and the hierarchy appraisal
discount.text: Record why infiltration cannot be used, whether any part remains practicable, and the evidence supporting the next destination. Where contamination is the constraint, assess practicable remediation together with the drainage design before discounting a higher destination. Testing is not automatically necessary where adequate initial evidence establishes that it is not needed.

links.label: RD-02 · Evidence for using a lower destination
RD-03 · Maximise each destination in order
RD-04 · Contamination is not an automatic reason to move down

IG-05 · No unacceptable instability, pollution or groundwater flooding

tests.question: Are detailed tests and ground evidence relevant to the proposed locations and depths?

investigate.result: Obtain the ground evidence needed for the proposed design
investigate.text: Check the Torbay test method, proposed locations and depths, and relevant seasonal groundwater evidence. Identify stability and pollution risks before accepting a design rate.

links.label: IG-02 · Test to BRE 365 at the feature location and depth
IG-04 · Establish wet-winter groundwater levels
IG-05 · No unacceptable instability, pollution or groundwater flooding
IG-13 · Groundwater protection and contaminated land

groundwater.question: Are groundwater separation, stability and pollution risks demonstrated?

risks.text: Read the feature sections and ground assessment together. A favourable infiltration rate alone does not establish safe groundwater separation, stability or pollution performance.

links.label: IG-03 · Keep 1 m above maximum groundwater
IG-05 · No unacceptable instability, pollution or groundwater flooding
IG-10 · Assess point infiltration within 5 m of structures

performance.text: Verify adopted rate, method, factor of safety and half-drain performance. Check the applicable requirements and recommendations for clogging protection, loading and exceedance. Record the finding against the evidence; this route does not approve a soakaway.

links.label: IG-07 · Do not rely only on point infiltration below 1×10⁻⁶ m/s
IG-08 · Half-empty within 24 hours
IG-09 · Use the Torbay factor of safety

discharge.title: Which discharge criteria apply?
discharge.intro: Keep the national event and volume tests separate from the applicable local criteria.

destination.question: Where is the proposed discharge going?

ground.text: Use the infiltration checks for the proposed system. Identify any positive overflow or alternative discharge route and assess its applicable criteria separately.

links.label: IG-01 · Prove infiltration with site testing

IG-09 · Use the Torbay factor of safety

tidal.result: Assess the receiving-water exception and local context
tidal.text: Read the national exception for tidal or sea discharges, then assess tide-locking, receiving conditions, pollution, local controls and necessary agreements. Do not assume a coastal location creates an unrestricted outfall.

links.label: RV-08 · Tidal or sea outfalls
FE-07 · Surcharged outfalls and flood-locking
WQ-08 · Outfall hierarchy

unknown.text: Follow the destination hierarchy and identify the receiving system, route, capacity, rights and required agreements before selecting design discharge criteria.

volume.question: Is the volume discharged to surface waters or sewers in the developed 1% AEP, six-hour event greater than greenfield runoff for the same event?

higher.result: Use the increased-volume national branch, then compare local criteria
higher.text: National clauses 3.18 and 3.19 use the greater of the 50% AEP greenfield rate and 3 l/s/ha for the relevant rate tests. Check the contributing area and baseline, then compare applicable local event-specific greenfield criteria and the Q10 ceiling. Record source differences and any agreement.

links.label: RV-03 · 50% AEP limit
RV-04 · 1% AEP limit: volume test
RV-05 · Compare the applicable national and local limits
RV-06 · Check proposals relying on the published 1.5 l/s minimum
RV-07 · Brownfield sites: check the greenfield expectation

lower.result: Use the no-increase national branch, then compare local criteria
lower.text: The national 50% AEP test uses the greater of its greenfield rate and 3 l/s/ha. Clause 3.20 uses the greater of the 1% AEP greenfield rate and 3 l/s/ha for the 1% test. Compare applicable local criteria separately and record the governing basis.

links.label: RV-03 · 50% AEP limit
RV-04 · 1% AEP limit: volume test
RV-05 · Compare the applicable national and local limits
RV-06 · Check proposals relying on the published 1.5 l/s minimum
RV-07 · Brownfield sites: check the greenfield expectation

missing.text: The 1% AEP national limit cannot be established from peak-rate figures alone. Compare greenfield runoff volume with the developed volume discharged to surface waters or sewers. Distinguish runoff generated from the volume remaining after interception, reuse or infiltration. Check the entire area potentially draining to the system and the correct model inputs.

application-stage.title: What evidence is needed at this stage?
application-stage.intro: Use a feasible strategy at outline and trace later detail back to the permission, strategy and conditions.

outline.result: Establish that the strategy can be delivered
outline.text: Check destination, constraints, land, levels, space, receiving capacity and lifetime delivery. Identify later detail explicitly. A condition should not stand in for evidence that the strategy is feasible.

full.text: Trace applicable standards through investigations, calculations, drawings, agreements and maintenance arrangements. Check that revisions and inputs agree across the package.

reserved.result: Start with the outline permission and approved strategy
reserved.text: Compare the detailed layout, drainage design and relevant conditions with the established strategy. Investigate changes that affect feasibility, capacity or the approved basis.

condition.text: Identify each relevant part of the condition and the drawing, calculation or agreement that satisfies it. Keep the approved strategy and subsequent revisions together.

small.result: Choose proportionate evidence for the actual planning route
small.text: Check the Torbay proforma scope, validation requirements and drainage risks. Establish which matters the route permits the council to consider. Application size alone does not remove a substantive requirement.
